points.text: Headline baseline Q-HeteroFL is author-built and weak, not state of the art.
Gains over Standalone and Vanilla QFL near zero; 'consistently outperforms' unsupported.
Loss, KL term and test-time ensembling confounded; no ablation; baseline readout unstated.
Ansatz, design and depth selected on test accuracy; no validation split.
'Shot-efficient' claim never measured; training analytic.
'Within 3% on QPUs' holds for one device, 100 points, no hardware baseline.
Ancilla design claimed confirmed on hardware but never run.
Higher early-layer gradient norms by construction; trainability claim unsupported.
Runs share data, test set and initialization; no seeds or CIs.
Test set size exceeds official splits; provenance unclear.
'Up to 12.4%' is actually the average gain.
Classifier count L-1 inconsistent with Eq. 1 and Table 7.
Training and evaluation not under device noise models.
No practical rule for choosing depth per device.
Cost accounting qualitative; no shots, wall-clock or cost figures.
Only binary tasks with 10 PCA features and small IID data.
No classical model reference.
Benefit of federation not demonstrated; no non-IID or small-data regimes.
Links to early-exit networks and error mitigation not discussed.
Privacy claimed as motivation but not analysed.
Headline claim inconsistent with Table 2; gain only versus own baseline.
Results small-scale for ICLR: binary, 10 qubits, five IID clients.
No limitations section.
Need for federation not shown; no regime where federation helps.
Table 2 dense; layer/depth/capacity terminology inconsistent.
Logits wording, FedAvg citation year, section reference.
Main contribution is DepthFL transplanted; 'first-of-its-kind' overstated; readout not compared to ensembles.
Claim that QFL ignores device heterogeneity contradicted by cited noise-aware QFL works.
Gradient-norm result is known local-cost effect; deeper circuits untested.
'State-of-the-art' wrongly applied to authors' own baseline.
Citation slips and conflated sentence.
Ansatz, designs, layer count chosen on test accuracy.
'Consistently outperforms' contradicted; federation adds little over Standalone.
'State-of-the-art' baseline is authors' own; no tuning.
Ensemble readout and KL confounds unablated.
Hardware claims overstated: one QPU, 100 points, Ancilla never run.
Gradient-norm trainability claim by construction and unsupported.
Shot efficiency unmeasured; noise absent from training.
'Up to' vs 'on average' 12.4%.
Possible Fig. 8 value inconsistency.
Section 3 conflates classical and quantum FL.
Test size larger than class-pair test splits.
Experimental gains very limited.
Scalability not studied.
Results limited to basic classification tasks.
Only binary MNIST/Fashion-MNIST; no multiclass or harder datasets.
No convergence theory or analysis of KL coupling.
Data encoding pipeline under-specified in main text.
Baselines weak or self-implemented, inflating gains.
Method limited to binary classification.
Unclear how ansatz yields all layer outputs in a single shot.
No classical baseline.
Approach heuristic; no convergence or bias-variance analysis.
Fairness gaps from rarely updated layers not quantified.
No comparison with communication-efficient FL methods.
Limited ablations; hyperparameter sensitivity unclear.

P.summary: Headline baseline author-built and weak; mislabeled state of the art.
'Consistently outperforms' unsupported; parity with simple baselines.
Federation benefit not shown; no non-IID.
